day_shape: 56 items: CENTCOM confirms US destruction of Chah Bahar surveillance tower and denies IRGC al-Tanf claim, IRGC/Sepah threatens CENTCOM naval units and claims strikes on Kuwait HIMARS and US tankers, UK formally proscribes IRGC support, rial hits record 1.92m/USD.

threads.label: US-Iran maritime and base exchanges
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari surveillance tower on 16 July and denied Iranian claims of an attack on al-Tanf Garrison in Syria that had been reported by IRGC via state media. Kepler data cited by Defa Press showed only eight ships transited the Strait of Hormuz in the past day.

threads.label: IRGC threats and claimed counter-strikes
threads.summary: Sepah Navy Command said via IRIB and Defa Press that US movements were under surveillance and warned CENTCOM naval units were approaching 'zero hour', while IRGC Statements 23 and 24 claimed destruction of HIMARS platforms in Kuwait, a long-range radar and US tanker aircraft. Khamenei's office said American bases in the region 'must be shut down', and Defa Press claimed satellite images showed US jets evacuating Al-Udeid to Saudi Arabia and Israel.

threads.label: UK moves against IRGC networks
threads.summary: Britain formally designated the IRGC under national security powers, making public support punishable by up to 14 years, and Counter Terrorism Policing charged a 39-year-old man with assisting Iran's intelligence service. Both actions were reported on 17 July by Iran International and the Jerusalem Post.

threads.label: Iran economy and domestic pressure
threads.summary: Iran International reported the rial hit a record 1,918,000 to the dollar on the open market and that moderate voices are criticising hardline confrontation as war costs mount. The Health Ministry said 38 Iranians had been killed and over 400 injured in recent US strikes, per Defa Press.

threads.label: Israel operations in Gaza and Lebanon diplomacy
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Hamas Khan Younis company commander Anas Mahmoud Ahmed Hamdan, who they said had held Israeli hostages, while an IDF interceptor was launched at a 'false identification' over southern Gaza with no actual attack. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul proposed an EU-mandated force to replace UNIFIL in Lebanon.

events.title: On July 16, U.S. forces successfully destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower, part of a maritime surveillance network along Iran’s Gulf of Oman coastline used for decades by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to track and target commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The destruction of the tower directly degrades IRGC’s ability to coordinate attacks on innocent civilian crew members. Furthermore, the strike protects freedom of navigation in regional waters for all vessels, except for ships attempting to violate the ongoing U.S. naval blockade against Iran.

events.title_en: Kepler: Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has reached its lowest level: Data released by Kepler company shows that ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has decreased over the past day such that only eight ships have passed through this area. American aggression against Iran in the Persian Gulf region has caused disruption to ship movement in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has repeatedly stated that it controls the strait and ships must only pass through the safe route designated by Iran. The consequences of using alternative routes that provide an opportunity for American military intervention in the region are the responsibility of violating ships.

events.title_en: Maritime incident off southern Yemeni coasts: Detention of a ship in Al-Mukalla: The UK Maritime Trade Operations organisation announced that it has received reports of a maritime incident at a distance of 65 nautical miles south of Al-Mukalla city in Yemen. According to the report from the British body, unidentified persons without permission boarded a ship whilst passing through the eastern section of the Gulf of Aden. The UK Maritime Trade Operations organisation also advised all ships to pass through the area with caution and report any suspicious activity to the organisation. Some news sources reported that forces of the Houthi movement in Yemen have taken control of this ship.

events.title: Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media
events.summary: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is amending its regulations to change the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period, and additional changes to admission and extension requirements. This final rule will provide additional protections and oversight of these nonimmigrant categories and will allow DHS to better evaluate whether these nonimmigrants are maintaining status while temporarily in the United States. This final rule provides amendments to the proposed rule covering this topic that was published in the Federal Register on August 28, 2025.
